Subject: Residency mapping + deletion handoff for CloudMarket listing

Hi Evelyn / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward the public listing in CloudMarket, our compliance team asked for a concise mapping of where customer data will live when customers select AWS vs GCP vs Azure regions, and — critically — how deletion requests are executed end-to-end.

Can you share a short Q&A or operational runbook that covers the following?
- Per-cloud residency mapping (S3/GCS/Blob equivalents + region names)
- Retention defaults and how customers can override retention via the Marketplace UI/contract
- Deletion request flow: who (CloudMarket vs Redwood) triggers deletion, timelines, confirmation artifacts
- Any cross-region replication or backups that require special handling

We need this to validate our security checklist and to include in the listing documentation. I attached our current template (residency_template.xlsx) — feel free to place your answers there or send a short write-up.

Thanks,
Anita
Anita Sharma
Senior Product Manager, Marketplace Integrations
CloudMarket Inc.

Subject: Re: Residency mapping + deletion handoff for CloudMarket listing

Hi Anita — really appreciate the template. I started a short operational Q&A and attached a draft mapping matrix. High level answers below; see the attachment for the per-region specifics.

Quick answers:
- Residency: For customers who pick an AWS/GCP/Azure region via CloudMarket, their inference request data and model usage metadata live in our customer-specific tenant in the selected region. We use native object storage (S3/GCS/Blob) in each cloud and configure region-specific service endpoints; no cross-region writes by default.
- Retention: Default token-level logs are retained for 30 days; embeddings/long-term artifacts default to 90 days unless a contract specifies otherwise. Customers can request longer retention via contract; we surface a UI toggle for partner-managed listings (CloudMarket) — see item 3 below.
- Deletion flow: When CloudMarket triggers a deletion through the Marketplace API, we receive a signed callback. Redwood executes a multi-step deletion: invalidate cache, remove tenant keys, delete objects from bucket, scrub backups and KV cache entries, then emit a signed deletion receipt. Typical SLA for full deletion across primary stores is 72 hours; we aim for 24–48 hours when not blocked by legal holds.
- Backups/replication: We do not replicate customer data across regions unless replication is explicitly enabled in the customer contract. Snapshots for HA may exist for a limited window (24–72 hours) and are included in the deletion lifecycle.

Next steps: Can we schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow to walk through the matrix and mark any exceptions for your partners? I propose 11:00–11:30am PT.

Attachments: residency_mapping_matrix.xlsx (draft), redwood-data-retention-policy.pdf

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Technical Partnerships (Marketplace)
Redwood Inference

Anita — a couple of operational clarifications from infra:

- Encryption: Customer objects are encrypted with per-tenant keys. For Marketplace listings, we support two modes: customer-managed CMEK (if requested by the buyer) or Redwood-managed keys by default. If CMEK is used, deletion includes key revocation which renders objects unrecoverable; we still perform object deletes for metadata cleanliness.
- Deletion confirmation: We produce a signed JSON receipt with timestamps for each store (object store, KV cache, audit log). We can post the receipt back to a CloudMarket webhook or attach to the DocuSign package if you prefer.
- Edge-case: For customers who enable cross-region failover, deletion must be coordinated; we mark those entries as 'replication-enabled' in the matrix and require explicit acceptance.

I'll add these notes to the matrix and flag any regions where the object naming differs (some Azure storage account conventions).

Ben
Director, Partner Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

- API contract: please confirm the exact POST payload CloudMarket will use to trigger deletion and the signing method (e.g., HMAC + shared secret or OAuth client assertion).

Marissa — can you help confirm whether CloudMarket will accept the signed JSON receipt posted to our webhook or if you need a different artifact for the listing page?

Subject: Re: Residency mapping + deletion handoff for CloudMarket listing

Quick technical answers to Paul's questions:

- SOC 2 evidence: yes — we can produce redacted deletion receipts that include operation IDs, timestamps, and SHA256 hashes of deleted object paths. PII is redacted. We keep an audit trail in our internal ledger for 12 months.
- Emergency deletion SLA: 48 hours for primary stores (object store + KV cache + search index). Backups/snapshots aimed at 72 hours due to snapshot rotation timing; we will include the 72-hour worst-case in the public listing but commit to a typical 48-hour operational run.
- API contract: CloudMarket will POST a signed payload: {action: "delete", tenant_id: "<id>", request_id: "<uuid>", requested_by: "<email>", signature: "<hmac>"}. We recommend HMAC using a per-partner shared secret; OAuth client assertion is possible but would add token exchange latency. I linked the draft spec in our Drive.

Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ResidencyPlaybook (matrix + sample receipts), Jira-RIF-789 (deletion-api-spec).

Karthik
Senior Engineer, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
